plan: Given the common knowledge of rationality and a single round, the optimal bidding strategy converges to bidding slightly above the expected value of the second highest bid. Since values are between $0 and $49, the expected value of the highest of the other two bids is approximately (2/3) * 49 = $32.67. However, because it is a single round, and we want to maximize profit, we should bid conservatively. My value is $22. I will bid slightly above the midpoint between my value and 0, to try and win at a low cost.

Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges towards bidding your value multiplied by 2/3. This is because any bid above that point risks overpaying, and any bid below risks letting the item go for less than its worth. Since this is round 1 with no history, I will implement this strategy. My value is $34, so 2/3 * $34 = $22.67. I will round this to the nearest tenth.

Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges towards bidding your true value. However, a slight underbid is optimal to avoid overpaying. Since this is round 1, and there's no history, I'll bid slightly below my value to attempt to win at a lower price. I will bid $9.50. This aims to secure the item if others bid low, while avoiding overpayment if others value it highly.
